s: The Velamas who were intruders into the economic life of Palnadu dominated by the Reddis were defeated and driven out in the
Damerla family of Velama tribe/caste ruled which of the following regions in Andhra Pradesh?
In which war did the dominant Reddys defeat and expel the Velamas who penetrated into the economic life of Palnadu?
x:
After the decline of the Kakatiya Empire, several regional kingdoms emerged in Andhra Pradesh, among which the Reddi Kingdom and the Recherla Velama Kingdom became two powerful political forces. Both dynasties frequently competed for control over fertile territories and strategic trade routes. The Battle of Bhimavaram was fought between the Reddi rulers and the Velamas. In this battle, the Reddis achieved a decisive victory and successfully drove the Velamas out of the Palnadu region, thereby restoring their authority over the area. The victory greatly strengthened the Reddi Kingdom and enabled it to consolidate its political influence in Coastal Andhra. It also checked the expansionist ambitions of the Recherla Velamas for some time.
Hence, the correct answer is
Option (2).
n: Result – Victory of Reddi rulers over the Velamas
Importance – Strengthened Reddi control over Palnadu

s: Who led the liberation movement after the fall of the Kakatiyas?
x:
After the fall of the Kakatiya Kingdom in 1323 CE, the Telugu country came under the control of the Delhi Sultanate. The movement to liberate the Telugu region from Sultanate rule was led by Musunuri Prolaya Nayaka, who united several Telugu chiefs and successfully expelled the Delhi Sultanate from large parts of Andhra and Telangana. He laid the foundation for the Musunuri Kingdom, which was later strengthened by his cousin Musunuri Kapaya Nayaka, who recaptured Warangal from the Delhi Sultanate.
Hence, the correct answer is
Option (1).
n: Leader of Liberation Movement – Musunuri Prolaya Nayaka

s: "Andhra Suratrana" is the popular title of whom?
x:
Anavema Reddy, one of the prominent rulers of the Reddy Kingdom, bore the title "Andhra Suratrana." The title literally means "Protector (Sultan) of Andhra" and reflects his role in defending Andhra territories and strengthening the Reddy kingdom after the decline of the Kakatiyas.
Hence, the correct answer is
Option (2).
